question.text: Trishul Angel Fund (Sub-category of Cat I AIF) invests in early-stage start-ups. Per the Revised Angel Funds framework (SEBI (AIF) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2025 w.e.f. Sept 9, 2025), which of the following is CORRECT?

answer.text: Minimum investment per investee is INR 50 lakh; maximum INR 50 crore
Angel Fund may invest unlimited amounts, subject only to the 25% single-investee cap
Investment by an Angel Fund shall not be less than INR 10 lakh and shall NOT exceed INR 25 crore in one investee company; lock-in 1 year (6 months if exit to third party)
Minimum investment is INR 2 crore (same as general AI framework)

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Chapter III-A of SEBI (AIF) Regulations and SEBI Circular of Sept 10, 2025: investment by an Angel Fund in a single investee shall be MIN INR 10 LAKH and MAX INR 25 CRORE (including follow-ons). Lock-in is 1 YEAR; reduced to 6 MONTHS if exit is via sale to third party (not promoter/buyback). Additional rules: (i) at least 5 AIs onboarded before first close, (ii) each investment must have ≥2 AI contributors, (iii) cannot invest in start-ups with group turnover > INR 300 crore, (iv) Sponsor/Manager continuing interest 0.5% of investment or INR 50,000 whichever higher. **The Trap:** Options A/B/D invent figures. The 25% single-investee cap applies at Cat I/II level but Angel Funds have their own bespoke INR 10 lakh / INR 25 crore floors and caps. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests Angel Fund in detail. Angel Funds are a Cat I sub-category, so XIX-D's Cat I/II scope covers them. Distinct from venture capital funds (VCF) which have 75% investable-funds deployment rule in unlisted equity of VCUs. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Angel Funds have no public listing allowed, can only raise from AIs, and trigger specific disclosure at each investment level — not at corpus level (unique treatment under the specific-DD land-border rules). Structure each investment round like a club-deal with term-sheet archive per investment.
